The therefore-clause at 49:2 turns to sentence: “behold, the days come” (web:Jer.49.2), through to “then Israel will possess those who possessed him” (web:Jer.49.2), closing not on the neum participle -- which stands mid-verse at the therefore-clause's own opening, נְאֻם יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.49.2, byte tier) -- but on the perfect verb form אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.49.2, byte tier), “says Yahweh.” A vocative shift follows at 49:3, “Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is laid waste! Cry, you daughters of Rabbah” (web:Jer.49.3), addressing the cities directly, continuing through the taunt at 49:4 into a terror pronouncement at 49:5 whose divine-title stack נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת (oshb:Jer.49.5, byte tier), “says the Lord, Yahweh of Armies,” stands mid-verse rather than at the verse's own close; the sentence runs on past it to its own end, וְאֵ֥ין מְקַבֵּ֖ץ לַנֹּדֵֽד (oshb:Jer.49.5, byte tier), “there will be no one to gather together the fugitives,” which is where this row's own span ends. What actually marks the row's rear seam is not a closure formula at 49:5 but the discourse pivot opening the following verse, וְאַחֲרֵי כֵ֗ן (oshb:Jer.49.6, byte tier), “But afterward” (web:Jer.49.6), turning the oracle from judgment to restoration.
